branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR carrier affine-incidence audit

assumptions: Circuit model is nonuniform fan-in two Boolean SIZE, with XOR implemented at linear overhead.
The constants gamma_i=<b_i,SAT|_{U_N}> over F_2 may be hardwired as nonuniform advice.
Bad inputs are corrected by equality tests of cost O(E_N N).
The source lower bound being audited is C(H_N^oplus)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} for infinitely many N.
definitions: source object: H_N^oplus(x)=xor_{j<=M} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on x in {0,1}^N, with M=N^q and query length L=(log N)^d.
target object: SAT on length-L formulas, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly if the source lower bound survives the polylog substitution bridge.
controlled interface: nonadaptive generated XOR of M=N^q SAT queries through a shared query-transcript generator G_N of size at most N^rho.
target-preserving condition: d>1 and max{q,rho}<1+epsilon, so every fixed polynomial SAT circuit exponent contributes only N^{q+o(1)} gates.
parity incidence vector: p_x(y)=#{j:G_N(x,j)=y} mod 2 over the generated universe U_N.
affine-incidence sketch: basis vectors b_1,...,b_K in F_2^{U_N} and coefficient functions a_i(x) with total circuit size A_N such that p_x=sum_i a_i(x)b_i outside E_N bad inputs.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no target-preserving compiler from unrestricted SIZE(m^k) to o(m)-juntas; parity supplies a small-circuit falsifier.
steps: Let f_m=SAT_m and attempt to prove SIZE(m^k) lower bounds through exact essential variables.
The syntactic compiler gives every size-s fan-in-two circuit at most 2s essential input variables.
Thus a valid transfer would require E(SAT_m)>2m^k.
But E(SAT_m)<=m for every m-bit function, so the required inequality is impossible for k>1.
Trying to pad SAT to length n=m^beta only changes the ceiling to E<=m while the target threshold becomes n^k, worsening the mismatch.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a route obstruction, not SAT hardness. It only shows exact-junta evidence cannot reach polynomial-size lower bounds beyond the linear threshold.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: exact-junta threshold audit

assumptions: Circuit size counts fan-in-two internal gates; changing conventions only changes the constant in 2s.
The lower-bound claim is exact, not average-case, unless an explicit approximate-junta compiler is separately supplied.
The SAT slice length used by the source measure is the same length used in the target SIZE(m^k) threshold.
definitions: source object: the m-bit truth-table function f_m, with motivating instance f_m=SAT_m or a padded SAT slice, and source measure J_0(f_m)=minimum exact junta size.
target object: nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean circuits SIZE(s) on the same m-bit input length, or a restricted class C equipped with an explicit junta compiler.

controlled interface: translate each target circuit of size s into an exact J_C(s)-junta; for unrestricted fan-in-two circuits J_C(s)<=2s because at most two fresh input variables can enter per internal gate.

target-preserving condition: the source lower bound must prove J_0(f_m)>J_C(m^k) on the unpadded target length; if J_C(m^k)>=m the transfer is nonvacuous only for a restricted target with a smaller certified compiler threshold.

For fan-in-two SIZE(s), the bridge threshold is J>2s; for SAT on m input bits this is vacuous for s=m^k with k>1, since every m-bit function is an m-junta.

definitions: Delta(f,Junta_J)=min_h Pr_x[f(x) != h(x)], where h ranges over J-juntas.

steps: Start with a low-D carrier image and a known easy anchor A_m, hoping that large cumulative edit volume along the construction path forces a hard endpoint.
Construct the nonuniform circuit for an endpoint T by hardwiring A_m and the final symmetric-difference edit set E(T,A_m), giving size C(A_m)+O(m|E|).
Observe that the number of candidate anchors, ranks, or path branches is irrelevant once the fixed endpoint circuit is chosen.
Try to rescue the argument by requiring large distance from A_m only.
Find the gap: T may be close to a different easy circuit B, so hardness requires a global anti-ball statement over all subthreshold B, not a rooted path-volume statement.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-level obstruction and a sharper falsifier for source proposals; it does not construct the required hard row and does not prove P != NP.

assumptions: A is a Boolean function on m bits with unrestricted circuit size C(A) <= 2^{xi m+o(m)}.
T differs from A on at most R <= 2^{eta m+o(m)} input points.
Circuits are nonuniform, so the nearest root and the edit list may be hardwired for a fixed row.
MCSP no-side threshold is s_m=2^{epsilon m}, with constant epsilon>0.
definitions: source object: E-uniform low-image MCSP certificate source S_m emitting truth tables T in {0,1}^{2^m}, with canonical distinct-image rank and no advice.
target object: unrestricted circuit lower bound for an E language obtained by rank-input multiplexing, with exponent delta after kappa padding.
controlled interface: canonical unranking plus sequential table evaluation within 2^{O(m)} time; no subthreshold local decoder or nonuniform length selector.

target-preserving condition: at least one emitted distinct row must satisfy C(T)>2^{epsilon m}; rooted edit descriptions, easy anchors, and rank indices may not themselves give circuits below that threshold.

equations.valid_when: Valid when T is obtained from a fixed easy root by explicitly hardwiring the changed input locations and output overrides.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repairs the previous rooted-volume accounting by removing beta or D from the individual nonuniform circuit upper bound; strengthens the source-side falsifier while leaving the established carrier-to-E extraction intact.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Rooted edit leakage has max-exponent accounting: if an emitted truth table T differs from an easy root A on R positions, then T has a nonuniform circuit computing A plus hardwired exceptions. Hence any subthreshold rooted ball around any easy center is a valid falsifier for MCSP no-side soundness; the number of possible centers or low-image ranks does not add to the circuit-size exponent for an individual row.

assumptions: The source is intended to certify unrestricted MCSP hardness, not only distance from a named root.
The verifier cannot enumerate all size-2^{epsilon m} circuits inside the E extraction budget.
The row family has distinct-image entropy D and remains no-advice.
definitions: For a circuit B of size b and radius r, Ball(B,r) is the set of truth tables differing from B on at most r inputs.
A global anti-ball certificate for T at epsilon rules out membership in Ball(B,r) for every unrestricted circuit B with b+O(mr)<2^{epsilon m-o(m)}.
The certificate must be sparse and non-large; dense constructive avoidance is a natural-proofs falsifier for this route.

equations.valid_when: Valid when correction circuits are implemented by equality tests against changed m-bit inputs and unrestricted gates are allowed.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns rooted-edit intuition into a precise global source obligation: excluding a single anchor or measuring path volume cannot certify row hardness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A rooted-volume certificate is insufficient unless it excludes all subthreshold easy centers. To certify C(T)>2^{epsilon m}, the source must prove that T is not in the O(2^{epsilon m}/m)-radius rooted ball around any circuit of size below 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}.

assumptions: The target lower bound is for unrestricted nonuniform circuits computing truth tables on m-bit inputs.
The transfer uses row hardness before multiplexing; it does not charge the circuit for discovering the row.
definitions: Rank entropy D is the logarithmic number of emitted distinct images divided by m.
Center entropy beta is the logarithmic number of candidate roots divided by m.
Unrestricted circuit lower bounds allow arbitrary constants hardwired into the circuit for one fixed row.

equations.valid_when: Applies after the hard row is embedded into a multiplexed E language with Dm rank bits and uniform unranking.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates source soundness accounting from extraction accounting; prevents smuggling index costs into an unrestricted row lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Center count, rank entropy, and path branching affect E-uniform unranking costs but not the nonuniform circuit complexity of a fixed emitted truth table. Therefore beta+D or beta+eta accounting is invalid for MCSP row soundness unless the target is a uniform or indexed model, which this route is not using.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if we produce an E-uniform sparse low-D source and a valid non-large certificate that some emitted row avoids all rooted balls with C(B)+O(mr)<2^{epsilon m}.

dependency_updates.description: Refined the circuit upper bound to C(T)<=C(A)+O(mR), with exponent max(xi,eta); center entropy and image entropy are not charged to fixed-row nonuniform circuits.
A viable source must certify distance from every subthreshold unrestricted circuit, not merely from a named anchor or construction path.
The multiplexed carrier transfer remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) after a genuinely hard row is certified.
Dense constructive bad-ball avoidance would be natural-like; the surviving object must be sparse, non-large, no-advice, and circuit-sensitive.

falsifiers: Subthreshold rooted ball falsifier: T=A plus at most 2^{eta m} edits with C(A)<=2^{xi m} and max(xi,eta)<epsilon.
Center-count overcharge falsifier: adding beta, D, or rank-search cost to an unrestricted fixed-row circuit is invalid.
Single-anchor certificate falsifier: distance from the construction root does not rule out closeness to another easy center.
Smooth path with cancellations falsifier: large cumulative edit count need not imply large final Hamming distance from any easy circuit.
Lex-first global safe row falsifier: if implemented by dense constructive search over all small circuits, the repair is either outside E or collides with natural-proofs largeness.
Local or interval decoder falsifier: any subthreshold indexed access profile still yields small circuits for emitted rows.

gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The current branch is blocked by explicit source construction, and the new issue is quantitative: whether edit radius, not path length or center count, controls MCSP soundness against unrestricted circuits.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each m, take an easy anchor A_m such as parity or 0^N, emit a low-D family of tables T_{m,j}=A_m xor E_{m,j}, where each E_{m,j} flips exactly R=2^{eta m} positions chosen by a sequential certificate; then test whether this can be a no-side GapMCSP carrier at threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: An E-uniform, non-large, non-natural global anti-ball certificate for at least one emitted row, plus canonical low-D unranking, before the thought experiment can support the carrier-to-E lower-bound transfer.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The edit-radius exponent eta, crossing below and above epsilon while keeping D, kappa, and the verifier budget fixed.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 53 corrects the rooted-volume accounting: for unrestricted MCSP row hardness, a circuit may hardwire the chosen easy center and final edit list, so the leakage exponent is max(xi,eta), not beta+eta or D+eta. This strengthens the falsifier for proposed sources and identifies the real next obligation as a global anti-ball certificate. The established carrier extraction is still valid only conditionally and gives no direct proof of P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Formalize a tiny-D aggregate of candidate rows and test whether pairwise anti-ball constraints can certify one hard row without lex-first search, dense largeness, or subthreshold ranked decoding.
